# Postmortem: Checkout outage, 2026-09-29

**Duration:** 14:03–18:05 UTC (4h 02m) · **Severity:** SEV-1 · **Status:** resolved, remediations in progress

## Summary

`order-service` exhausted its Postgres connection pool after `tax-service`, a synchronous downstream dependency, slowed from ~80 ms to 30+ s per call. `order-service` made that call inside an open database transaction with no HTTP timeout, so every slow call pinned a connection. About 60% of checkout requests failed for four hours.

## Impact

- ~60% of checkout requests returned 503 or timed out; about 41,000 orders failed.
- Health checks used the same pool, so healthy instances were restarted, deepening the outage.
- No data was lost or corrupted.

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:58 | `tax-service` deploys a release containing an unindexed query; p99 latency climbs to 30 s+. |
| 14:03 | `order-service` pool hits 50/50 on all instances; 503s begin. |
| 14:07 | Pool-exhaustion alert pages on-call, who suspects the database. |
| 14:40 | Postgres failover performed, with no improvement. |
| 15:20 | Pool size raised from 50 to 200; Postgres hits `max_connections` and other services start failing. |
| 15:45 | Pool change reverted. |
| 16:45 | Thread dumps show all request threads blocked in the `tax-service` HTTP call. |
| 17:05 | `tax-service` team engaged and confirms latency regression. |
| 17:30 | Hotfix deployed to `order-service`: 2 s timeout on the tax call. Errors drop to ~15%. |
| 17:50 | `tax-service` release rolled back. |
| 18:05 | Error rate back to baseline; incident closed. |

## Root cause

`order-service` opened a transaction, called `tax-service` over HTTP, then wrote the order. The HTTP client used its default timeout (infinite). When `tax-service` slowed, each in-flight request held a database connection for the full duration of the call. With 50 connections per instance and normal traffic, the pool was fully pinned within five minutes.

## Contributing factors

- **Misleading signal:** the only alert was pool exhaustion, which pointed at the database. There was no latency alert on the `tax-service` call, costing about 2h 40m of diagnosis.
- **Shared pool for health checks:** starved checks triggered restarts of instances that were otherwise fine.
- **Client retries:** three retries without backoff tripled load on the already slow `tax-service`.
- **No kill switch:** the tax call could not be disabled or degraded without a deploy.
- **Harmful mitigation:** raising the pool size spread the failure to other services sharing the database.

## Remediations

| Action | Owner | Due | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Set 2 s timeout on the `tax-service` client | Orders | Done | Hotfix shipped |
| Move the tax call outside the transaction | Orders | 2026-10-12 | In progress |
| Add circuit breaker with cached-rate fallback | Orders | 2026-10-19 | Planned |
| Replace retries with capped exponential backoff and jitter | Orders | 2026-10-19 | Planned |
| Remove DB dependency from the liveness check | Platform | 2026-10-12 | Planned |
| Alert on downstream p99 latency and pool wait time | Observability | 2026-10-16 | Planned |
| Lint rule: no outbound HTTP inside a transaction; require explicit timeouts | Platform | 2026-10-30 | Planned |
| Add query-plan check to `tax-service` CI | Tax | 2026-10-23 | Planned |
| Runbook: pool exhaustion means check thread dumps before touching the DB | SRE | 2026-10-09 | Planned |

## What went well

Paging fired within four minutes, and the hotfix took 45 minutes from diagnosis to production.
